❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) & Local CLI Guide

Q: Why was this tool created?

  • Finding out which Google Cloud services, APIs, machine series, or GPUs are available in a specific GCP region—or conversely, finding all regions where a specific GCP service is deployed—often requires cross-referencing multiple documentation pages. This tool harvests all official GCP location feeds, zone hardware matrices, and Google Discovery REST APIs into a single local, cached, instant-search application.

Q: How often is the data refreshed, and how are API quota issues prevented?

  • By default, the dataset is refreshed once per day (24-hour TTL = 86,400 seconds).
  • All UI interactions, searches, region comparisons, and CLI queries read from the local cache (data/cache/gcp_catalog.json) and pre-rendered static HTML files in dist/—making zero external API calls during normal usage.
  • When the daily harvest runs, ResilientFetcher enforces a token-bucket rate limit, checkpoints every individual API specification to disk, and automatically retries any 429 / 403 / 5xx responses using exponential backoff with full jitter.

Q: How do I run the application locally?

# 1. Start the local web server (serves dist/ + REST API + daily auto-refresh thread)
python3 server.py --port 8080

# 2. Or open the static HTML files directly in any browser:
open dist/index.html

# 3. Query from the terminal using cli.py (uses the local 24h cache):
python3 cli.py service "Vertex AI"
python3 cli.py service alloydb
python3 cli.py region us-central1
python3 cli.py region asia-south1
python3 cli.py compare us-central1 europe-west1 asia-south1

# 4. Force an immediate live re-harvest & static site rebuild:
python3 cli.py refresh --force
Disclaimer: The data on this application is harvested once daily from public Google Cloud Location feeds, Compute Zone/GPU matrices, and Google APIs Discovery REST specifications (`discovery.googleapis.com`) and served locally via static HTML & JSON cache.
